result.summary:
Static review only; no checks executed.

HELPER (cookInstructionBlocks) — reproducible logic bug:
The abbreviation/initial guard in _splitSentences uses `word.length == 1` to detect "a single initial" before a period, but `_wordBefore` extracts any run of `[A-Za-z0-9]`, so a lone DIGIT immediately before a period is also treated as a protected initial. Concretely, for input like "Serve 4. Enjoy!" or "Repeat step 3. Add the salt.", the digit-check for decimals (digitBefore && digitAfter) fails because the character after the period is a letter, so control falls through to the abbreviation/initial guard, which incorrectly matches `word.length==1` for the digit and suppresses a legitimate sentence split. This contradicts the doc comment's stated intent ("a single initial") and is a genuine correctness defect distinct from the documented ellipsis/decimal/abbreviation guards — it silently glues two sentences whenever a sentence ends in a lone digit. No existing test in the supplied suite exercises a single-digit sentence ending, so this is unconfirmed by the test run but is derivable by hand-tracing the code. Fix: restrict the length==1 guard to alphabetic characters (e.g. check `RegExp('[A-Za-z]').hasMatch(word)`).

Minor/cosmetic: the built accessibility label `'Step ${step.stepNumber}. ${step.text}. Tap to go on.'` always appends a period after `step.text` even when the stored text already ends in terminal punctuation (as in the chili fixture's third sentence), producing a doubled `..`. The supplied test only asserts `.contains(fullText)`, so it won't catch this; it's a real but low-severity announcement-quality issue, not a functional regression.

No other reproducible defects found by inspection in the splitting algorithm: ellipsis, decimal (digit-digit), ratio/clock-time (no colon matched), quoted-punctuation, CRLF/bullet line handling, and the non-whitespace-preservation invariant all trace correctly against the supplied fixtures and tests, including the U.S./e.g./i.e./abbreviation cases.

UI: The left-alignment, 560pt/24pt paragraph styling, 17pt focused progress text, removal of the oversized numeral, and the single collapsed Semantics node (avoiding double announcement) all match the described requirements as coded. The `scrollActions` heuristic (`maxHeight<400 || textScale(18)>27`) is a plausible but unverified proxy — it does not account for whether `onStartTimer` is present (an extra button), so a step with a running-timer button plus Mark-done at a moderate (but not extreme) text scale and borderline height could get a very compressed (not overflowing, just cramped) content-scroll area; this is a UX concern, not a proven crash/overflow, and isn't covered by the size/scale matrix (which only varies text scale, not timer-button presence at intermediate scales).

Missing coverage (not bugs): non-ASCII capital-letter sentence starts (e.g. "É...") are not exercised — by design such boundaries stay conservatively unsplit since `_boundaryStart` only recognizes ASCII A–Z/0–9/quotes; very-long-text performance stress is untested; the parent wiring that passes `focused: true/false` into `_Progress` isn't visible in this packet, so left-alignment/top-anchoring wiring can't be confirmed end-to-end from these files alone; the new 320×568@3x completion-label regression and native walkthrough are explicitly pending and unverified here.

Repair reviewed by manual trace against helper logic and the two added regression tests. The fix narrows `_initial` to `^[A-Za-z]$` (letters only), so a lone digit before a sentence-ending period (e.g. 'step 3.', 'Serve 4.') no longer matches the initials guard and correctly participates in decimal/abbrev checks then falls through to normal boundary detection, producing the expected split. Traced 'Set the dial to 1.5. Stir well.': first dot correctly caught by digitBefore&&digitAfter decimal guard (kept as 1.5), second dot's look-back word is '5' which now fails both abbreviation and (letters-only) initial checks, so it correctly splits before 'Stir'. The separately added `_numberedPrefix`/`prefixEnd` guard correctly identifies a leading '1.', '• 1.' etc. and skips exactly that dot as a boundary while leaving all other punctuation in the line to normal sentence-boundary logic — traced against both list-marker regression tests including the bullet+number case and the two-line numbered-list case, matching expected output. Multi-digit numbers before a period (e.g. 'Cook for 10.') correctly still split since the initials regex requires exactly one letter character, so they were never mis-protected. Quoted-punctuation, ellipsis, abbreviation, ratio/time/decimal, and comma-non-split behaviors are untouched by this diff and traced correctly on their respective existing tests. No interaction was found between the new prefix-skip logic and the closing-quote/space-after/boundary-start checks that run after it — prefixEnd only ever causes an early `continue` for the one designated list-marker dot. No character-preservation, ordering, or line-break regressions are introduced; the change is additive/restrictive (narrows a regex, adds one bounded skip condition) and does not alter any other branch. No actionable defects found in this repair; the doubled-punctuation and ASCII-fallback items are correctly out of scope per the brief. Accept the fix as correct with no regressions identified.

Traced the updated helper against all listed scenarios by hand. The core fix — refreshing `prefixEnd` via `_numberedPrefix.matchAsPrefix(line, start)` immediately after each split advances `start` to `j` — correctly re-anchors the numbered-prefix check at the new block start instead of using the stale line-start-only value. Verified for '1. Chop. 2. Fry. 3. Serve.' that each of '2.' and '3.' is now recognized as a list marker at its block start and skipped as a sentence-ending dot, producing the three expected attached blocks, matching all 26+ tests including inline numbered items, sentence-ending numbers (with and without decimals), multiline numbered markers, bullet+number markers, and decimal/ratio/abbreviation guards untouched by this change. `matchAsPrefix(line, start)` anchors only at the given index rather than rescanning from 0, satisfying the 'no rescanning entire prefix' requirement. No substring/slicing logic was altered, so text and order preservation (join+strip-whitespace round trip) is unaffected — only which sentence-ending dots are skipped as list-prefix dots changed, and skipping never consumes or reorders characters. No source/UI files outside the helper were touched. No defects found; the fix is sound and consistent with the documented design (numbered-prefix recognized at each block start, not just line start). One pre-existing, out-of-scope ambiguity noted only for completeness, not as a defect: a leading pattern like '1.5. Add flour.' at a block start would have its '1.' segment matched as a list-prefix by `_numberedPrefix.matchAsPrefix`, since the regex greedily matches the first digit run before the first literal dot; this behavior is unchanged by this diff (it already existed for line-start prefixes before the fix) and is not part of the reported regression or current test suite, so it is not blocking.

Reviewed images 1–4 (24pt dark, 26pt dark, final 24pt light ingredients scrolled, final 24pt small/3x scrolled with timer).

Font-size recommendation: 24pt. Comparing image1 (24pt) vs image2 (26pt), both remain legible and well within the card width with comfortable wrap points, but 26pt tightens the gap between the step-3 paragraph and the 'Start timer' button and pushes the last line of paragraph 3 ('...rendering fat.') noticeably closer to the button edge, reducing the breathing room that currently separates body copy from controls at 24pt. 24pt also keeps better visual proportion against the unchanged 22pt ingredient rows, 18pt actions, and 17pt progress label — at 26pt the step text starts to visually dominate the 'Mark done'/'Next' button labels in a way that flattens the hierarchy rather than reinforcing it. Recommend 24pt.

Hierarchy: 'Step 1 of 2' progress label (17pt, muted) reads clearly as metadata above the body text in both dark comparisons; step body text is the clear focal point; button labels (18pt) remain visually subordinate to body copy, which is correct for a directions-first screen.

Paragraph spacing: The three paragraphs in image1/2 have consistent, even spacing between them — no orphaned single lines, no cramped paragraph boundaries. Line spacing within paragraphs also looks even and consistent at 24pt.

Alignment: Left alignment is consistent across headline, body paragraphs, and the progress label; no ragged or inconsistent left edges observed.

Legibility/reflow (light theme, image3): Text wraps cleanly with no truncation, no overlapping elements, no clipped descenders/ascenders. The 'For this step' ingredient callout box has clear internal spacing separating its label from the two ingredient lines, and sits with adequate margin from both the paragraph above and the timer button below.

Responsive controls (image4, small/3x, scrolled with active timer): 'Mark done' button scales to a large two-line label that remains fully contained within its rounded button bounds with no clipping. The active timer chip ('H... 5:59') with pause/dismiss icons is legibly rendered and fits its row without overlap into the Back/Next buttons below. Back/Next buttons remain proportionate and legible at this scale. No visible overflow, clipping, or icon collision in this static capture.

No concrete defects (clipping, truncation, overlap, misalignment, unreadable contrast) found in any of the four images; observations above regarding 26pt spacing tightness are a preference-level comparison supporting the 24pt recommendation, not a functional defect.

Cannot assess native scroll momentum, timer countdown behavior, or touch-target responsiveness from static images — those require interactive testing, which is out of scope here.

Independent visual pass over the 4 supplied captures (desktop 1280x800; short-instruction phone 390x844; 3x-text small phone 320x568 top-of-scroll; scrolled 8-ingredient phone). No true visual defects identified. Findings:

1) Desktop (1280x800): Directions/step counter/ingredient panel/buttons all render within a centered max-560 column, left-aligned text, top-anchored. Spacing, wrapping, and button stack look correct. No clipping or overflow.

2) Short-instruction phone (390x844): Short directions text left-aligned/top-anchored as specified; large empty space above the button stack is expected behavior for short content, not a layout bug — buttons remain bottom-anchored correctly.

3) 320x568 @3x, top-of-scroll: Only 'Step 1 of 2' and the start of the direction text ('Heat 1 tbsp') are visible before Back/Next, with the ingredient panel and Start-timer/Mark-done buttons pushed below the fold. This is consistent with expected scrollable behavior at extreme text scale, not truncation — the text is not clipped, it's simply below the viewport in this single static frame. No ellipsis/cutoff artifacts on the visible text itself. Per the stated constraint, a static capture can't confirm native scroll reachability of the off-screen controls; that requires interactive/device verification, which is outside what these 4 images can prove and is already covered by the passing focused step/timer/back walkthrough on Mac.

4) Scrolled 8-ingredient phone (ingredient panel view): All 8 ingredients wrap cleanly with consistent line spacing, no overlap or clipping, buttons fully visible at bottom. Matches the separate review's finding of no clipping in the 3x completion/timer state.

Type sizing (24pt directions / 22pt ingredients / 17pt progress) reads as proportionate and legible across all four captures; no evidence contradicts the prior 24-over-26pt recommendation. Left-alignment and top-anchoring are consistent everywhere text is present. Width appears capped near 560 on the wide desktop view.

No rewrites of original wording were needed or observed — text content matches source in all captures.

Verdict: ACCEPT. No blocking visual defects found in these 4 states. Only note (not a defect) is that reachability of controls below the fold in the 3x/320-width scenario is inferred from scroll design intent rather than directly proven by a single static top-of-scroll frame; this is a testing-coverage note, not a rendering flaw, and is already substantively supported by the passing automated/interactive suites cited.
